claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd like to know about my child, Alex. He's 13 and lives with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So we're assessing eligibility for **Alex, who is 13 years old and lives with you**.

Before I can make a determination, I need to gather a bit more information. Let me start by reading the eligibility criteria to ensure I ask you the right questions.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I have the eligibility criteria. Based on the information you've provided, Alex is 13 years old and lives with you. According to the rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and live in the UK.

I have a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not living in the UK at the moment. I'm abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for letting me know. That's an important detail. Let me read the specific guidance about living abroad to understand how this affects your eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see the guidance mentions that you may be able to get Child Benefit if you live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant, but it doesn't specify which countries. To help clarify your situation:

**Which country are you currently living in?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not say exactly which country, but it's not the UK. Does it matter which specific country I'm in?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a fair question. Yes, it does matter which country you're in, I'm afraid. The guidance states that you "may be able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in certain countries," which means eligibility depends on the specific country.

However, I understand your preference not to disclose the exact country. In that case, let me ask this in a slightly different way:

**Are you living in an EEA (European Economic Area) country or Switzerland?**

This would help me determine if you might fall under one of the specific eligibility categories mentioned in the rules.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not in an EEA country or Switzerland.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Given that you're living outside the UK and not in an EEA country or Switzerland, I need to understand your situation better to determine eligibility.

The guidance indicates that you may be able to get Child Benefit if you live in "certain countries," but it doesn't specify which ones in the information I have access to. Since you're not in an EEA/Switzerland country, I have an important question:

**Are you a Crown servant (such as working for the UK government abroad, in the civil service, armed forces, or similar official capacity)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 13 years old and lives with you
- You are living abroad (outside the UK)
- You are not in an EEA country or Switzerland
- You are not a Crown servant

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and **you live in the UK**. The guidance does mention that you "may be able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in certain countries," but since you're not in an EEA/Switzerland country and not a Crown servant, you don't fall into the specified exceptions.

However, before I make my final determination, I want to check if there are any other circumstances that might apply. Let me ask:

**Are you receiving any UK benefits such as Income Support, Jobseeker's Allowance, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any UK benefits.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. I now have enough information to make my assessment regarding Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

Based on the eligibility criteria I've reviewed, the fundamental requirement is that you must be living in the UK to qualify for Child Benefit (unless you fall into specific exceptions like being a Crown servant or living in certain approved countries). Since you are living abroad, outside the UK, in a country that is not an EEA country or Switzerland, and you are not a Crown servant, you do not meet the basic residency requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

The main reason is the residency requirement. Child Benefit is designed for those living in the UK, and while there are some exceptions (such as being a Crown servant or living in certain approved countries), your current circumstances don't fall into those categories.

If your situation changes in the future – for example, if you move back to the UK, or if you need more detailed information about whether your specific country might qualify – I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office directly, as they may have more detailed information about eligibility in specific countries.
